A chronic lung condition goes unmedicated alongside frequent ER and police contact during eleven months of vehicle living.
Frequent ER and police contact and an inability to maintain hygiene or regular meals suggest mounting risk despite no diagnosed chronic condition.
A chronic heart condition with a lapsed blood-pressure prescription poses real risk, tempered by ongoing work, sibling support, and an engaged shelter nurse.
Advanced arthritis leaving this 71-year-old needing help to bathe and dress, combined with ongoing financial exploitation by a relative, marks significant frailty and dependency.
A diagnosed chronic liver disease left unaddressed for years, paired with total social withdrawal and refusal of services, signals quiet but real medical risk.
An untreated dental infection and four ER visits in six months, layered onto mounting debt and depressive withdrawal, suggest escalating but not yet severe physical risk.
Advanced arthritis and a hip injury limit daily function, but stable income, medication adherence, and consistent support meaningfully offset the risk.
A worsening chronic stomach condition goes unmedicated, though stable routines and a supportive friend provide some buffer.
No health conditions and strong independent functioning are balanced against 14 months of unsheltered exposure and reliance on a strict daily survival routine.
No physical health issues are reported, but complete disengagement from work search and a joyless routine suggest emerging depressive risk without acute danger.
Financial stability and no health conditions limit physical risk, though grief-related withdrawal and loss of routine are notable concerns.
Eighteen months outdoors with no health conditions, no violence, and steady informal income indicate relatively low but not negligible risk.
Seven months in a car with no health conditions, no violence, and an active family support network point to comparatively low vulnerability.
Chronic but stable seasonal homelessness with no health conditions, steady income, and no safety incidents reflects low acute risk despite the lifestyle's precarity.
Two months in a car with solid income, no health issues, and a clear housing plan show early-stage, low-severity homelessness.
A brief first-time shelter stay with steady work, savings, no health issues, and a concrete housing plan reflects the lowest vulnerability in this group.
